purpose: give the scenario model a governed set of scenarios and payoffs to model, in place of three divisors
features_criteria_rules_actions_scenario: actions: continue as planned, accelerate, rebaseline, descope, claim. scenarios: base, supply disruption, weather-driven delay, design change wave, labour shortage. criteria carried per cell: cost outcome, duration outcome, quality outcome
target_or_ground_truth: the payoff in each cell, expressed as cost at completion and duration at completion, plus a stated scenario probability
minimum_sample_size: 5 actions by 5 scenarios = 25 cells, one matrix per project type
recommended_sample_size: 5 actions by 8 scenarios, three project types, so 120 cells
class_balance_or_alternative_coverage: every action must appear against every scenario; scenario probabilities must sum to one
train_validation_test_split: not applicable: this is a designed decision structure, not a fitted model
expert_elicitation_and_uncertainty_field: the payoffs and the probabilities must be recorded as elicited from a named panel with the elicitation date and the number of experts, and marked as designed rather than observed
ground_truth_outputs: expected value, expected regret and reliability per cell
known_answer_fixture: a 3 by 3 matrix with payoffs 10/20/30, 20/30/40, 30/40/50 and probabilities 0.5/0.3/0.2 gives expected values 17.0, 27.0 and 37.0, minimax regret 20 on the first action, and the healthy action must be reachable, which is the property the ranking and regret modules currently fail

purpose: give the ranking methods more than one alternative, which is what makes a CRITIC weighting and a MARCOS utility meaningful at all
features_criteria_rules_actions_scenario: alternatives: the projects or courses of action being ranked. criteria: cost performance, schedule performance, document risk, safety, quality, procurement exposure. each criterion carries a direction (benefit or cost), an ideal and an anti-ideal
target_or_ground_truth: the ranking the method should produce, computed independently from the matrix by a published worked example
class_balance_or_alternative_coverage: the alternatives must span the range of each criterion so no criterion has zero variance across alternatives, which is the degenerate case this run found
expert_elicitation_and_uncertainty_field: each criterion needs a stated direction and a stated normalisation; the CRITIC weights must be derivable from the matrix rather than supplied
ground_truth_outputs: the CRITIC weights, the TOPSIS closeness coefficient and the MARCOS utility degree for each alternative, hand-computed from a published worked example carried beside the matrix
known_answer_fixture: a 3 by 3 matrix (0.9,0.8,0.7 / 1.0,0.9,0.8 / 1.1,1.0,0.9) with equal weights gives standard deviations across ALTERNATIVES rather than within a row, which is the correction the current code needs; the top-ranked alternative must be the one dominating on every criterion, a property the current ranking module violates

purpose: supply the population of comparable completed projects a reference class forecast is drawn from
features_criteria_rules_actions_scenario: project_id, sector, delivery_method, contract_value_at_award, final_cost, planned_duration_days, actual_duration_days, region, year_completed, complexity_band, and the derived realised cost and schedule overrun ratios
target_or_ground_truth: the realised overrun ratio per project, which is the distribution the forecast is a percentile of
recommended_sample_size: 200 completed projects per class, three classes
class_balance_or_alternative_coverage: the class must span the overrun distribution, not only the tail; at least fifteen per cent of projects must have completed UNDER budget or the debiasing factor is one-sided
train_validation_test_split: not applicable: this is a reference population, not a trained model; if it is ever used to fit, hold out twenty per cent by completion year
expert_elicitation_and_uncertainty_field: each project needs its comparability basis recorded (which attributes matched) and a data-quality flag, because a reference class is only as good as its matching rule
ground_truth_outputs: the empirical percentiles of the overrun ratio (P10, P50, P80, P90) per class, computed directly from the population
known_answer_fixture: a class of 20 projects with overrun ratios evenly spaced from 0.90 to 1.28 in steps of 0.02 has a median of exactly 1.09 and a P80 of 1.214, both checkable by hand from the sorted list

purpose: supply the design structure matrix a rework propagation analysis traces a wave through
row_object_grain: one ordered pair of design elements
features_criteria_rules_actions_scenario: design elements: architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, civil, controls. each ordered pair carries a dependency strength and a rework probability
target_or_ground_truth: the propagated rework volume from a stated initiating change, computed by matrix powers
minimum_sample_size: 7 elements, so a 7 by 7 matrix with 42 off-diagonal cells
recommended_sample_size: 12 elements, three matrices for three project types
class_balance_or_alternative_coverage: every element must both depend on and be depended on by at least one other, or the matrix decomposes and the propagation is trivial
expert_elicitation_and_uncertainty_field: each cell needs the elicitation source and a confidence, and the matrix needs a stated convention for whether rows depend on columns or the reverse, which is the single most common error in this method
ground_truth_outputs: the propagated rework at each iteration and the convergent total, computed as the Neumann series of the matrix
known_answer_fixture: a 2 by 2 matrix with off-diagonals 0.3 and 0.2 and an initiating wave of 1.0 on the first element propagates 0.3, then 0.06, then 0.018, converging to 1/(1 - 0.06) = 1.0638 times the initiating wave, which is checkable in closed form
